boltzmann.narrative: Sampled 2,000 forward paths for XOM over 5 trading days as a weighted mixture of 12 generator rules, seeded by 25 historical analogs that all closed on or before 2019-09-13 -- closest: XOM 2008-10-29 (+15.6%), XOM 2008-11-28 (+17.0%), XOM 2008-10-10 (-20.0%). The coarse-grained result: median -0.2%, 90% interval [-3.6%, +4.6%]; the scenario prior (heuristic-fallback (LLM disabled by caller)) contributed an expected +0.0% 5-day drift on the 45% of paths that accept drift, and a 1.05x width multiplier on all of them. Changing the generator rule moves the median by 1.1 percentage points, which is our honest uncertainty about the rule itself rather than about the noise draw.

invariants: INVARIANT (91.7% of 144 generators): the 5th percentile is not worse than -5%.
rule_dependent: RULE-DEPENDENT (47.9% of 144 generators): the 5-day median return is NEGATIVE. Driven by the `drift_prior` axis (eta^2=0.31; scenario=63.9%, sign_only=63.9%, zero=63.9%, unconditional=0.0%). NOT a finding, and NOT skill.

RULE-DEPENDENT (47.9% of 144 generators): more than half the paths finish down (P(down) > 0.50). Driven by the `drift_prior` axis (eta^2=0.31; scenario=63.9%, sign_only=63.9%, zero=63.9%, unconditional=0.0%). NOT a finding, and NOT skill.
RULE-DEPENDENT (27.1% of 144 generators): P(down) exceeds 0.55. Driven by the `conditioning` axis (eta^2=0.58; same_ticker=75.0%, cross_ticker=6.2%, same_era=0.0%). NOT a finding, and NOT skill.
RULE-DEPENDENT (54.9% of 144 generators): the 95th percentile is better than +5%. Driven by the `resampling` axis (eta^2=0.47; iid=93.8%, stationary=60.4%, block=10.4%). NOT a finding, and NOT skill.

RULE-DEPENDENT (78.5% of 144 generators): the ensemble's centre is small next to its width (|median| < 1/3 sigma). Driven by the `resampling` axis (eta^2=0.21; iid=91.7%, stationary=91.7%, block=52.1%). NOT a finding, and NOT skill.
note: Ran 144 of the frozen 144-generator grid for XOM as of 2019-09-13 at 1000 paths per rule (144,000 paths total) in 0.87s wall clock (0.78s for the grid itself). No generator failed. MEASURED sign agreement on the median: 52.1% (69 down / 75 up / 0 flat), so reducible=false at the frozen 0.90 threshold. Median band -0.46% to +1.33%; P(down) band 0.000 to 0.664. Variance across the grid, one-way eta^2 per axis. MEDIAN: analog_selection=0.010, conditioning=0.214, drift_prior=0.634, resampling=0.027 (interaction+noise 0.116). P(DOWN): analog_selection=0.007, conditioning=0.060, drift_prior=0.545, resampling=0.030 (interaction+noise 0.357). HEADLINE, and it fell out of the numbers rather than a docstring: the `drift_prior` axis dominates BOTH the median (eta^2=0.634) and P(down) (eta^2=0.545). Where you put the centre of the distribution is the answer; how you retrieve analogs and how you resample them barely move it. That is the same rule-dependence already measured as +14.8% CRPS lift collapsing to -4.5% once demeaned, and a Boltzmann ensemble cannot see it by construction. Monte-Carlo noise floor at 1000 paths: re-seeding one fixed rule 5x moves the median across a 0.02% range (sd 0.01%) and P(down) across 0.030 (sd 0.011). Compare any axis level-mean spread against that before believing it. Axis level-mean spread vs that noise sd, median: analog_selection 0.13% = 12.8x noise; conditioning 0.56% = 53.0x noise; drift_prior 0.93% = 88.8x noise; resampling 0.20% = 19.3x noise. Anything under about 2x is not distinguishable from sampling noise at 1000 paths per rule and should not be read as an axis effect. Axis level-mean spread vs that noise sd, p_down: analog_selection 0.030 = 2.7x noise; conditioning 0.078 = 7.0x noise; drift_prior 0.228 = 20.5x noise; resampling 0.054 = 4.9x noise. Anything under about 2x is not distinguishable from sampling noise at 1000 paths per rule and should not be read as an axis effect. Boltzmann single-generator comparison (kept in the response on purpose): median -0.18%, P(down) 0.552 over 2,000 paths. Note it is not literally one rule -- the shipped generator is itself a 12-rule mixture at FIXED weights, which averages the rule uncertainty away into a single distribution. That averaging is exactly what the grid above refuses to do. LLM OFF: the scenario prior is the generator's deterministic keyword heuristic, not model reasoning. 144 LLM calls would be slow, non-reproducible, and would vary a fifth thing the contract did not freeze. Only properties holding under >=90% of generators appear in `invariants`. Anything that flips is in `rule_dependent` with the axis responsible, and is not skill. Known degeneracy in the frozen grid, stated rather than pruned: analog_selection=ticker_only and conditioning=same_ticker express nearly the same restriction, so 12 of the 144 points are close to duplicates. The grid is frozen at 144 and every point was run; the eta^2 for those two axes is correlated as a result. WARNING: STRUCTURAL COLLAPSE: 16 of 144 generators produced fewer than 20 distinct terminal values (fewest: 9). This is resampling=block at block_len==horizon with a tiny analog pool -- a circular rotation of a whole window has the same sum. Their P(down) can read 0.000 or 1.000 and is not a probability. They are LEFT IN the grid: excluding them, or moving block_len off the horizon, would be pruning a frozen axis to improve a number. WARNING: DRIFT-AXIS COINCIDENCE: these drift levels produced numerically IDENTICAL medians and are therefore the same generator on this request -- scenario==sign_only; scenario==zero; sign_only==zero. Cause: the event text implies no direction (implied_direction='unknown') so the deterministic prior returns zero drift for every regime and sign_only has no sign to carry. The drift axis is effectively narrower than 4 levels here, which INFLATES its variance share. Read the drift eta^2 below with that in mind.

axis_mapping.analog_selection: generator `corpus=` param; tfidf_magnitude uses the generator's own shipped scorer, the other three pre-rank here (added: 3 rankers)
axis_mapping.conditioning: generator `corpus=` param, pool filter (added: the era filter)
axis_mapping.drift_prior: generator GeneratorRule.drift_mode: scenario->prior, zero->neutral, unconditional->analog. added: sign_only = neutral base + a constant added to cumulative log return, magnitude = the generator's own measured analog drift, sign from the event text only
axis_mapping.resampling: generator GeneratorRule.block_len: iid->1, block->horizon. added: stationary = geometric-weighted mixture over block lengths, run through the generator's own rule-mixture machinery (per-path, not per-block, geometric length)
axis_mapping.held_fixed: vol_anchor='blend' and analog_scope='universe' on every one of the 144 -- neither is a frozen axis, so letting them vary would add a fifth dimension

mc_noise_floor.what_it_means: Re-seeding ONE fixed rule this many times moves the median by this much. An axis whose level-mean spread is not comfortably larger than this is not distinguishable from Monte-Carlo noise at 1000 paths per rule.

diagnostics.leakage_disclosure: The language model that proposes this forecast's scenario prior was trained on text published after 2019. Cutting the input data at 2019 does not cut the weights. For a famous event the model may be recalling the outcome rather than reasoning about it. This is why we report lift over a null model rather than raw accuracy, why the test set contains obscure events alongside famous ones and reports them separately, and why the LLM's influence in this generator is capped: it may set width and, on 45% of paths, a clamped drift. It may not emit a point prediction.

leakage_disclosure: Any LLM in this pipeline has read the post-2019 world. Cutting input data at 2019-12-31 does not cut the weights. We therefore report lift over a null model rather than raw accuracy, test obscure events alongside famous ones and report them separately, and say so here, in the product. See CONTRACT.md s8.
